chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every illness is from satiation (overeating), except for fever, for it arrives gradually.
ai.seo_question: What is the primary cause of most illnesses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies overeating as the primary cause of most ailments, distinguishing fever as an exception that arises gradually rather than from satiation. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Prophetic tradition of moderation in diet, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on physical health as a prerequisite for spiritual devotion. The distinction highlights the understanding that while digestive issues stem from excess, fevers often result from external or systemic factors requiring different management.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ibn Sinan, from the one who mentioned it,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Every illness is from the satiation apart from the fever, for it arrives gradually’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from ibn Sinan from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
’Every illness is because of overeating except, fever (infection) which enters the body.’”
